correctness.rationale: Direct substitution into the source exact RandProx-LC update gives u_next=(1−aI)u and x_next=−γ(1−aI/p)u. Conditional iid moments yield the exact q and c, with q<1 iff 0<a<2. Geometric summation yields J. Symbolic differentiation yields S_prime=2[(1−p)a²+pa−p]/[p²a²(2−a)²], whose numerator is strictly increasing. Its unique zero is a*=2sqrt(p)/(sqrt(p)+sqrt(4−3p)). G(p)<0<G(1), and direct asymptotic expansion proves the p^(-3/2) versus p^(-2) contrast. Standalone symbolic and complete finite rational checks corroborate all identities; they are not used to infer the infinite result.

originality.rationale: First-priority paper and close ProxSkip full-text sections were compared by mathematical implication, along with targeted published mathematical record searches. Known source results give a sufficient step bound and a Lyapunov-rate estimate. They do not state or obviously imply the exact nontrivial optimum of the accumulated primal squared-feasibility loss over a free RandProx-LC dual step; this includes a parameter regime beyond the source theorem and an asymptotically unbounded risk separation. An earlier equivalent unindexed scalar recurrence analysis remains possible, so the finding is a qualified best-knowledge priority judgment.
residual_risks: A prior equivalent calculation may appear in older or differently indexed stochastic fixed-point or random-coordinate splitting literature.
The conclusion is specific to exact-gradient scalar constrained quadratics and the chosen cumulative feasibility metric; no global novelty claim about randomized proximal methods is asserted.

value.rationale: The unique cumulative feasibility risk minimizer differs both from the generic sufficient dual step and from the fastest asymptotic dual contraction; an unbounded separation of risk scaling as p→0 is mathematically substantive for random-constraint enforcement. The exact scalar counterexample delineates where one should not confuse rate tuning, sufficient stability tuning, and integrated feasibility tuning; no claim of broad method superiority is made.
